observations: The OEM row describes an off-state low-side voltage classification with ignition synchronization, speed above 1,400 rpm, counter difference above nine and a 0.4-second interval.
The source labels coil B while the generic definition labels coil E. The article preserves that unresolved mapping without locating a physical cylinder or claiming a failed component.

observations: GM pages 849–850 require position error of at least 5 degrees and feedback below 50 degrees, with four failing seconds in a five-second window.
Relay and voltage eligibility plus valid feedback qualify the position interpretation; the monitor alone does not prove a failed valve or thermostat.

samples.method: Independent root review of complete article against Ford physical pages147–148; wording correction verified after author integration.
samples.result: One architecture wording clarification corrected; remaining sampled statements supported.
observations: Ford distinguishes invalid digital patterns from PWM frequency, duty-cycle and analog circuit criteria. The separate monitoring durations and architecture-specific intervals are preserved.

The source permits digital inputs and/or an analog circuit. The revised article now says analog-circuit faults apply on relevant designs, avoiding an assertion that every digital design must use an analog input.
